policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the clause with the explicit verb 'ravished,' distinguishing the ketiv reading r01 from the qere/base euphemism.
ASV's main text, 'the bright ones shall withdraw themselves,' uses a finite verbal predicate and thus distinguishes the ketiv reading r01; the alternative_rendering note does not decide the unit.
